title: Pyelonephritis – Children
summary: NICE Visual Summary available (see source). Refer to paediatric specialist urgently if child less than three months old or if a child of any age has signs of a more serious illness or condition (for example, sepsis). See NICE NG224 guideline on urinary tract infections in under 16s and NICE guidance on Pyelonephritis (acute): antimicrobial prescribing.
changeSummary: Initial transcription from Eolas Medical, Northern Ireland Primary Care Antimicrobial Guidelines (v5.119.0).
clinicalNotes: For true penicillin allergy NICE provides an alternative second choice (see visual summary in source).
Nitrofurantoin suspension may not be immediately available; guidance is available on using tablets or capsules in children if required.
See BNF for appropriate use and dosing in specific populations, for example, hepatic impairment and renal impairment, or for drug interactions.

components.dose: Child 1–11 months: 12.5 mg/kg BD, alternatively 125 mg BD; 1–4 years: 12.5 mg/kg BD, alternatively 125 mg TDS; 5–11 years: 12.5 mg/kg BD, alternatively 250 mg TDS; 12–17 years: 500 mg BD. Dose may be increased in severe infections – refer to BNFC
components.frequency: Twice daily or three times daily (see dose)

components.dose: Child 3–11 months: 0.25 ml/kg of 125/31 suspension TDS (dose doubled in severe infection); 1–5 years: 0.25 ml/kg of 125/31 suspension or 5 ml of 125/31 suspension TDS (dose doubled in severe infection); 6–11 years: 0.15 ml/kg of 250/62 suspension or 5 ml of 250/62 suspension TDS (dose doubled in severe infection); 12–15 years: 250/125 mg or 500/125 mg TDS

regimens.label: 2nd choice
notes: IV antibiotics required – refer to secondary care.

clinicalValidation.reviewNotes: Transcribed from Eolas Medical; not yet clinically validated.
